Arcade machines take tokens. Tokens are bought with euros at the converter machine or at the Token Exchange on the Hypernet, and unused tokens can be cashed back in.

Both quote the same rate.

the_workbench.title: The Workbench
the_workbench.description:
The Thinker is the general workbench: assembling and dismantling. The recipe is written on the item.

A recipe stays hidden until it has been made once, though common ones are on the board from the start.

Base materials come from dismantling the world: felling trees, mining rocks, breaking furniture, salvaging gear.

the_forge.title: The Forge
the_forge.description:
Every weapon and armour in the game is on the forge board from your first visit. Training decides what you can make.

Four tabs: what you can make now, what you lack materials for, what needs more training, and what this party has already forged.

Each item belongs to a trade: a robe is Tailoring, a wig is Wig Making, a rifle is Gunsmithing, a circuit coat is Electronics.

Every forged piece is unique and doesn't stack. Better training and better materials make better pieces.

Pick a finish from the swatches.

Smelt turns a carried piece back into some of its materials, more for a well made one.

The party switcher sets who forges and who earns the specialization points.

alchemistry.title: Alchemistry
alchemistry.description:
Every alchemy recipe is open from the start, for any class.

Copy a recipe onto a bench, then edit and run the bench. One recipe can run on two benches set up differently.

Success depends on skill. Meet every requirement and you never fail; fall short and failure becomes likely; go beyond and you get extra product.

Steps take game time, so a batch keeps going while you walk, work, travel or sleep.

A bench set to repeat buys its ingredients and starts again, and stops with a warning when you can't afford a run.

cooking.title: Cooking
cooking.description:
Cooking combines two recovery items into one. The first item's recovery is doubled and the second's is added, so order matters.

Cooking two of the same thing adds a random adjective instead, with a bonus or a penalty. The name is built from the first word of the first ingredient and the last word of the second.

Food has calories, fat and protein, and a cooked meal is worth what went into it.

brewing.title: Brewing
brewing.description:
Barrels ferment on the world clock. Load a barrel, leave it, and brewing and distilling proceed while you play.

It is the slowest crafting and needs no attention.

building_and_furniture.title: Building and Furniture
building_and_furniture.description:
The Build menu places furniture on tiles, snapped to the grid. Pieces can be crafted from materials, bought, and dismantled to recover them. Multi tile pieces are supported and some can be flipped.

Wall furniture goes on walls only, the upper tiles of ordinary furniture may overlap a wall but the lower tiles may not, and some terrain refuses furniture.

The Build menu is also where animals are bought.

farming.title: Farming
farming.description:
Any tilled soil can be farmed. Plants grow with time, season and weather.

They grow only in their seasons and rest outside them. Rain and storms speed growth, snow slows it, and greenhouses grow all year. A fully grown plant is harvested on the spot; the management menu opens only on plots still growing.

Tilled soil on generated maps can be farmed too, and some fields are already sown when you first arrive.

animals.title: Animals
animals.description:
Animals are bought in the Build menu and placed on a tile, then managed from the Assets screen as livestock to collect from, sell, or turn into a pet.

They grow from baby to adult over a set number of days, and adults produce at intervals: an egg, a pail of milk, a fleece.

Every animal has a company value that fills the party's social need when you interact with it, once per game day. Dogs, donkeys and roosters produce nothing and are kept for this.

beekeeping.title: Beekeeping
beekeeping.description:
A hive is a colony simulation. Queen, workers, nurses, guards, foragers and drones each have a lifecycle from egg through larva and pupa to adult and death. The comb is drawn as hexagons, and the colony produces honey, pollen, royal jelly and wax.

Seasons and weather act on it, disease and pests threaten it, and its mood and efficiency follow how it is kept.

procedural_artifacts.title: Procedural Artifacts
procedural_artifacts.description:
Artifacts are generated items, weapons and armour with rolled properties. They appear in loot, in vaults, at the end of adventures, and from certain rites.

One rite turns a party member into a weapon.

how_loot_is_rolled.title: How Loot Is Rolled
how_loot_is_rolled.description:
Random loot gets better as your party levels up, and harder places drop better loot.

Rarity follows price, and the same colours mark item names in the backpack, shops, rewards and containers.

Holy Patron Bunkers drop especially valuable loot.

containers.title: Containers
containers.description:
Containers hold items without limit, and each is unique to its map and event. Contents are generated from the categories the container declares, weighted by rarity.

The extradimensional container can be opened from anywhere and travels with the party, as do the holds of the camper and the car.

the_star_map.title: The Star Map
the_star_map.description:
The star map is a real time 3D view of the universe at several scales: the system you are in, the galaxy, the local group, the supercluster, the cosmic web and the observable universe. At system scale one unit is one astronomical unit, and bodies are drawn larger than life to stay visible.

Drag to orbit, wheel to zoom. Clicking a body selects it and offers what you can do: travel there, or land.

Planets have day and night terminators tracking their own star, independently turning cloud layers, atmospheres and rings. Star surfaces boil.

travelling_between_stars.title: Travelling Between Stars
travelling_between_stars.description:
Select a system and travel to it. The journey takes time and burns fuel, and fuel sets your range.

Only an ordinary fusing star can power a refuel. Main sequence stars of every class work; remnants, brown dwarfs and black holes do not. Refuel starts the pumps if you are parked at one, plots a short hop if there is one elsewhere in the system, and otherwise plots a course to the nearest system that has one.

On any map inside the ship the windows show where you actually are, and they streak and scroll while under way.

your_starship.title: Your Starship
your_starship.description:
The ship is generated. Hull, layout, plating, panel lines, livery, decals, lit windows and wear are all procedural, and the default appearance comes from your world's seed.

From the vehicle menu you can reroll the whole thing or step through individual traits and keep the rest.

Under way the crew tends one need at a time: a meal, a wash, a conversation, a game, a shift of sleep. Eating consumes food from the hold.

landing.title: Landing
landing.description:
In orbit you can land. Where landing sites exist you pick from a list; otherwise you touch down on the surface.

An alien surface is an explorable map, generated like Earth's but from a different palette, with dozens of alien biomes chosen by the type of world.

- encounters are not scaled to your party or your distance from home. The planet's own level decides, readable from its biosignature before you commit
- there is nothing to forage. Food comes from butchering local wildlife
- a body stripped of its resources stays stripped

Identified species go into the bestiary's alien page.

anomalies.title: Anomalies
anomalies.description:
Every star system with planets has at least one anomalous world, marked with a question mark.

Holding orbit over it offers to investigate, once only. What follows is a branching encounter written for that kind of world, paying out in a relic, in salvage, in a fight with something native, or in nothing.

It runs the same engine as the adventures on Earth's map.

what_is_out_there.title: What Is Out There
what_is_out_there.description:
Stars come in the real classes and in a couple of dozen exotic kinds, each with its own model: remnants, brown dwarfs, feeding X-ray binaries. Systems can be binary or hold several stars, each travelled to individually.

Black holes come in three weights, the largest bending the light around them and trailing a spiralling accretion stream. Rogue planets drift between the stars with no sun.

About twenty real nebulae sit at their real galactic coordinates, hand shaped: the Horsehead, the Orion Nebula, the dark nebulae. Dyson spheres exist.

Above the galaxy the map continues: local group, superclusters, cosmic web filaments and the shells of the observable universe.

Our own solar system is hand authored, with its twelve real bodies, its belts and a shell of orbital debris.

patron_worlds.title: Patron Worlds
patron_worlds.description:
Some worlds in other galaxies are named after the people who paid for the game. They are habitable and life bearing, they orbit exotic objects, they sit in nine planet systems where every planet is a different type, and they are listed in the star map catalogue under Patrons.

Each of those people also owns a hatch on exactly one world map square. It cannot be dismantled and nothing grows over it. Going down opens their Holy Patron Bunker: a great hall with strongrooms and a deep back chamber, filled with money and weapons, with loot weighted toward the most expensive items.

Hatch locations are encrypted in the game data.

the_night_sky.title: The Night Sky
the_night_sky.description:
A night sky chart, separate from the star map: a draggable, zoomable planisphere with stars sized by magnitude, constellations traced in gold, a right ascension and declination grid, and a Milky Way band.

Tab switches between constellation sets, European and Chinese, which trace different figures over the same stars.

the_hypernet_desktop.title: The Hypernet Desktop
the_hypernet_desktop.description:
The Hypernet is a simulated operating system of the period: desktop, taskbar, start menu, draggable and resizable windows, and a set of applications.

It has a virtual file system and registry, both saved inside your savegame, so written files and changed settings persist.

- WASD or arrows move the focus ring, Tab cycles
- Enter or Space activates
- Escape leaves a text field, then closes the window, then exits
- on a controller: d-pad navigates, A activates, B closes, the left stick is a free cursor

app_hypernet_explorer.title: App: Hypernet Explorer
app_hypernet_explorer.description:
The browser. Tabs with their own history, back, forward, stop, refresh and home, an address bar with autocomplete, a links bar, an explorer bar with search, favorites and history, find on page, view source, saving a page, downloads, print preview, zoom, encoding, a pop up blocker, mail and news, and a 404 gateway page that suggests alternatives.

Every page in the archive is a full document. Preferences, favorites, history and downloads live in the registry and are kept in your savegame.

app_my_computer.title: App: My Computer
app_my_computer.description:
The file explorer. It browses the virtual file system: drives, folders, My Documents, and everything you or an application has written.

Files open in whichever application owns them: a text file in Notepad, a saved web page in the browser.

app_notepad.title: App: Notepad
app_notepad.description: A plain text editor writing into the virtual file system. Notes typed here are saved in your savegame, can be reopened, and can be read by any application that reads files.

app_control_panel.title: App: Control Panel
app_control_panel.description:
Machine settings. Your party's statistics are presented as hardware specifications. Wallpapers, display settings and the rest of the configuration live here.

Changes are stored in the registry.

app_tv_guide.title: App: TV Guide
app_tv_guide.description:
The television listings, read from the broadcast database. Browse every channel, its cast and its programmes.

Selecting a programme plays its broadcast inline, a line every couple of seconds, without leaving the desktop.

The schedule regenerates every in game week and is fixed for that week.

app_the_object_index.title: App: The Object Index
app_the_object_index.description:
A catalogue of every item in the game, with a dossier for each.

The left page lists items by category, with a search box. The right page shows the dossier: identification, description, trade, physical properties, food values, composition and tags.

Randomize rewrites the description for this window only.

app_npolice.title: App: N€police
app_npolice.description:
The continental police portal, for settling your criminal record without waiting to be caught.

- case file: every charge with its fine, settleable one at a time or all at once
- self-report: confess something not yet registered, at half the usual fine
- custody: turn yourself in, or request a hearing before Eris

The custody options close the computer, because the cells and the courtroom are places on the map.

app_eurodemics.title: App: Eurodemics
app_eurodemics.description:
The public terminal of the continental epidemic observatory, reading the live outbreak grimorie.

- situation: outbreaks running, people ill, people dead, towns affected, and a readout of where you are standing
- outbreaks: every outbreak burning, each with its daily curve, redrawn at midnight, over the town by town table
- archive: outbreaks this world has closed, plus the epidemics and mass hysterias of the last century

app_artifact_analyzer.title: App: Artifact Analyzer
app_artifact_analyzer.description: Analyses procedural artifacts and reports what they actually do.

app_token_exchange.title: App: Token Exchange
app_token_exchange.description: Converts euros into arcade tokens and back, at the same rate as the physical converter machine.

the_hexphone.title: The Hexphone
the_hexphone.description:
The party carries a mobile phone: credit, contacts, call history, an inbox and a couple of built in games.

Calling a contact triggers what that person does when called. Incoming calls arrive with an answer or decline prompt.

Keypad digits dial and act as shortcuts, Enter selects, calls and opens, Escape ends and goes back.

Payphones share the same contacts and credit grimorie, but only place outgoing calls: no inbox, no games, no incoming calls.

television.title: Television
television.description:
Watch any television you find. Tuning to a channel puts you in its studio, where the cast performs the show. Shows with no cast are narrated.

Shows talk about your world: the history channel and the news cover what has actually happened.

The schedule changes every game week, and each show is different every time you tune in.

Adverts sell either products at their real price or a political message.

Watching a whole show raises the party's Fun, except for Technophobes, who lose Fun instead.

The channel guide is a teletext page.

the_radio.title: The Radio
the_radio.description:
Radios tune across AM, FM and EM bands. The stations are built from the music files the game ships with, so every track is somewhere on the dial.

Left and right change frequency, up and down change band, page up and page down scan, Enter marks a favourite. Between stations there is static.

The last station tuned is remembered.

music_and_sound.title: Music and Sound
music_and_sound.description:
Battle music is chosen in Options. Random draws a different track at the start of every fight, and None fights in silence.

Map music is fixed: one track per combination of biome, nation and time of day. Some music is generated live by a procedural system.

Each track is announced with its title and artist, as a notification or a drawn cassette.

Footsteps change with the surface underfoot.

diversions.title: Diversions
diversions.description:
The 3D games are simulations rendered through a retro shader, and most are played where you stand: the pool table, the basketball court, the bowling alley and the chess board are dropped into the scenery of the map you are on.

Playing anything feeds the whole party's Fun. Control hints are not printed; the keys are the ones you already use.

Two players can share almost all of them. Real time games let either player steer and turn based games become hot seat.

the_arcade_cabinet.title: The Arcade Cabinet
the_arcade_cabinet.description:
Arcade cabinets take tokens, bought with euros at the converter or on the Hypernet. A cabinet keeps high scores with letter entry and runs a demo when idle.

Each cart is a complete game, drawn in colour ASCII:

- Snake, against a red computer snake competing for the same apples
- Manpac, a pellet maze with three hunters and power pills that make them edible
- Hoppa, across roads and rivers to five home slots
- Astro Intruders, with destructible barriers
- Meteoroids, with splitting rocks and a wrapping screen
- Wallbreaker, with falling capsules
- Crawler, splitting when shot in the middle, with a spider that eats the mushrooms
- Bubble Pop, colours that stick and clusters that fall
- Boot sequence, a cabinet booting up and then a space to walk around in

bowling.title: Bowling
bowling.description:
A 3D bowling alley with real pin physics.

The camera follows the ball down the lane and cuts to the pins on impact.

Aim, power and spin use the same moving slider as pool and basketball.

pool.title: Pool
pool.description:
A nine foot table simulated in metres. Balls roll under cloth friction, throw each other off on impact, rattle in the jaws of a pocket and drop.

Aim, power and spin are set with the oscillating slider. The table is placed in the scenery around you.

basketball.title: Basketball
basketball.description:
A free throw shootout against a computer opponent on a half court.

The ball arcs, bounces off the rim and backboard, and goes in or misses.

chess.title: Chess
chess.description:
Full rules chess on a low poly 3D board. Every piece is a creature from the 3D battler system, dealt from the world seed, so one world always fields the same two armies: a bright one for White and a dark one for Black.

Two modes: normal chess and Chaos.

fishing.title: Fishing
fishing.description:
First person fishing. Fish, junk and hostile encounters are built by the same procedural battler system the battles use, so a Megalodon hooked in the lake is the Megalodon you then fight.

Aim by looking around. A ring on the water shows where the cast lands, then it is a tug of war between your line and the catch.

surfing.title: Surfing
surfing.description:
First person surfing. Waves break along the beach, and the whitewater swallows the wave behind.

The board pitches and rolls. Read where the wave is breaking and stay ahead of it.

the_shooting_range.title: The Shooting Range
the_shooting_range.description:
A first person target range. The weapons handle exactly as they do in battle.

The range lends you the weapon, so you can try one before buying it.

Only bows, thrown weapons and firearms are available.

the_horse_race.title: The Horse Race
the_horse_race.description:
A 3D turf course with rails, a starting gate, a winning post and a grandstand.

Each horse's look comes from its name, so a horse with the same name looks the same in every world.

The odds shown are fair.

the_monster_tournament.title: The Monster Tournament
the_monster_tournament.description:
A knockout monster tournament to bet on. Pick a fighter, bet tokens, and watch only your monster's fights.

The fights use the real battle rules, then play out in a 3D arena.

Betting does not change the outcome.

slots,_scratch_cards_and_tarot.title: Slots, Scratch Cards and Tarot
slots,_scratch_cards_and_tarot.description:
Slot machine: a cabinet whose reels are drums. Each symbol is a plate on a facet of a cylinder, so a spin turns the drum and a landing overruns its stop and springs back. The symbols come from the game's icon set.

Scratch cards: printed tickets rubbed panel by panel in any order, and the card can be turned in the light while you do it.

Tarot table: the deck riffles, the reader cuts it, the cards fly to their positions face down and turn one at a time.

the_piano.title: The Piano
the_piano.description:
A playable three octave keyboard, C3 to B5. It is played with the typing keyboard laid out as two manuals, whites on one row and blacks above, with a gamepad, or with the mouse. Keys light as they sound.

Playing it feeds the Fun need.

lockpicking.title: Lockpicking
lockpicking.description:
Picking a lock is a falling block puzzle: a key bit must fit into a partly packed keyway, and the lock's difficulty sets how hard the fit is.

Failure consumes a lockpick. A skeleton key skips the game and opens the lock outright.

Lockpicking opens locked doors and parked cars. Being caught at it is a crime.

hypertamer.title: HyperTamer
hypertamer.description:
A virtual pet on a monochrome LCD handset, drawn from the creature database and given a personality that changes how it behaves.

It runs on real time: it eats, sleeps, plays and can die of neglect, and time passes while the game is closed. Training minigames raise its stats and it grows accordingly.

the_card_game.title: The Card Game
the_card_game.description:
A collectible card game with a collection, a deck builder and duels.

A card is a monster, a weapon or a piece of armour from the game's database, printed with five stats, STR, WIS, DEX, PSI and CON, each from 0 to 13. Those numbers are percentiles against that card's own roster, not raw parameters. Equipment is bolted onto a monster already on the board and its values are added, clamped to 13.

A deck is 9 to 20 cards and may only hold copies you own. A player who never opens the deck builder is dealt the best legal deck their collection allows.

A duel is three by three. On your turn you either draw three cards or place one: a monster onto a free tile, or gear onto one of your own monsters, one weapon and one armour each.

When the last tile is taken, every monster looks at its four orthogonal neighbours, picks the weakest enemy among them and fights it. Every pairing is scored against one frozen snapshot of the board and all deaths land together. Most stats won takes the fight, an equal count destroys both. Whoever has more monsters standing wins, ties broken on the summed stats of the survivors.

Booster packs hold six cards from one pool, weighted so the last is never common.

Cards are also won by capturing a creature in battle. Capture picks the weakest creature still standing, helped by the caster's PSI against its own, and is impossible against anything more than ten levels above your median. Success adds the card and kills the creature, so the spoils still drop.

the_raman_scanner.title: The Raman Scanner
the_raman_scanner.description: A spectroscopy scanner that analyses the object you are facing: statues, paintings, masks, bookcases and library objects. It identifies the material, draws its Raman spectrum, and pays knowledge points.

the_periodic_table.title: The Periodic Table
the_periodic_table.description: A viewer for the periodic table, laid out as a book: the full grid on the left page, lanthanides, actinides and a set of esoteric elements that appear in no real table, with the selected element's description on the right.

hardware_store.title: Hardware Store
hardware_store.description: Salvaged steel, wood, nails, cable and the rest of what a Build or Thinker recipe asks for, sold over a counter instead of prised off a ruin. Every town of any size has one, and the stock is rerolled with the day.

esoteric_heavy_particles.title: Esoteric Heavy Particles
esoteric_heavy_particles.description: What a leyline is made of. Too heavy to travel far from the oil they surface with, heavy enough to bend an instrument on the way past. Measuring them is how a wizard tells a live leyline from a dead one, and how CERN spends its year.

cern.title: CERN
cern.description:
The ring under Geneva, turned from particle physics to the only physics that pays since the Falklands: esoteric heavy particles, and through them the leylines.

The one place on the continent where the Guild of Wizards and a payroll of atheists work the same corridor.

state_arcane_surge.title: State: Arcane Surge
state_arcane_surge.description: Increases magic power but consumes MP each turn. It raises INT by 50%, raises WIS by 50% and drains 10% of max MP every turn. It lasts 3-5 actions.

state_berserk.title: State: Berserk
state_berserk.description: Increases attack power but decreases defense and makes target attack randomly. It raises STR by 50% and lowers CON by 30%. The afflicted attacks anyone at random, ally or enemy. It lasts 2-4 actions.

state_bleeding.title: State: Bleeding
state_bleeding.description: Drains 10% of max HP every turn. Doesn't wear off on its own and lasts after battle.

state_blind.title: State: Blind
state_blind.description: It lowers accuracy by 50%. It lasts 3-5 actions.

state_burned.title: State: Burned
state_burned.description: Drains 10% of max HP every turn. Doesn't wear off on its own and lasts after battle.

state_charm.title: State: Charm
state_charm.description: The afflicted turns on their own side. Lasts 2-4 actions. A solid hit can break it early.

state_cold.title: State: Cold
state_cold.description: It lowers ice damage taken 50%, raises STR by 10% and raises fire damage taken 200%. It lasts 5 turns.

state_confusion.title: State: Confusion
state_confusion.description: The afflicted attacks anyone at random, ally or enemy. Lasts 2-4 actions. A solid hit can break it early.

state_shadow_veil.title: State: Shadow Veil
state_shadow_veil.description: Makes target harder to hit but also reduces their accuracy. It lowers accuracy by 40% and lowers how often it is targeted by 50%. It lasts 2-4 actions.

state_silence.title: State: Silence
state_silence.description: It seals a school of skills. It lasts 3-5 actions.

state_sleep.title: State: Sleep
state_sleep.description: It lowers evasion by 100%. The afflicted cannot act at all. It lasts 3-5 turns. A solid hit can break it early.

state_static.title: State: Static
state_static.description: It lowers thunder damage taken 50% and raises STR by 10%. It lasts 5 turns.

state_stun.title: State: Stun
state_stun.description: It lowers evasion by 100%. The afflicted cannot act at all. It lasts 1-2 turns.

state_unbalanced.title: State: Unbalanced
state_unbalanced.description: Target has a chance to fail their action at the end of each turn. It lowers accuracy by 30%. It lasts 1-3 actions. A solid hit can break it early.

state_vulnerability.title: State: Vulnerability
state_vulnerability.description: Lowers physical defence: CON down 50%. Doesn't wear off on its own and lasts after battle.

state_wet.title: State: Wet
state_wet.description: It lowers fire damage taken 50% and raises thunder damage taken 100%. It lasts 5 turns.

state_immortal.title: State: Immortal
state_immortal.description: It wards off Dead. It lasts 1-2 turns.

state_poison.title: State: Poison
state_poison.description: Drains 5% of max HP every turn. Doesn't wear off on its own, but walking it off works. Lasts after battle.

state_rage.title: State: Rage
state_rage.description: It raises STR by 50%. The afflicted attacks an enemy at random and cannot be commanded. It lasts 2-4 actions. A solid hit can break it early.

state_freeze.title: State: Freeze
state_freeze.description: Lowers evasion by 100% and seals skills. The afflicted cannot act at all. Lasts 3 turns.

state_paralysis.title: State: Paralysis
state_paralysis.description: It lowers evasion by 100%. The afflicted cannot act at all. It lasts 3 turns.

state_locked_on.title: State: Locked on
state_locked_on.description: Raises critical rate by 300%. Lasts 2-4 actions.

state_hp_regeneration.title: State: HP Regeneration
state_hp_regeneration.description: It restores 10% of max HP every turn. It lasts 4 turns.

state_mp_regeneration.title: State: MP Regeneration
state_mp_regeneration.description: It restores 10% of max MP every turn. It lasts 4 turns.

state_ap_regeneration.title: State: AP Regeneration
state_ap_regeneration.description: It restores 10% of max AP every turn. It lasts 4 turns.

state_magic_reflection.title: State: Magic Reflection
state_magic_reflection.description: It raises magic reflection by 100%. It lasts 5 turns.

state_protect.title: State: Protect
state_protect.description: It changes how the battler behaves. It lasts 1 turn.

state_provoke.title: State: Provoke
state_provoke.description: It raises how often it is targeted by 800%. It lasts 5 turns.

state_counter_attack.title: State: Counter Attack
state_counter_attack.description: It raises counter rate by 100%. It lasts 3 actions.

state_inspired.title: State: Inspired
state_inspired.description: Lowers MP cost by 75%. Lasts 5 turns.

state_hot.title: State: Hot
state_hot.description: It raises water damage taken 100%, raises STR by 10% and lowers petro damage taken 50%. It lasts 5 turns.

state_divine_shield.title: State: Divine Shield
state_divine_shield.description: Cuts every incoming element by 30% and makes critical hits impossible. Lasts 3-5 turns.

state_death_mark.title: State: Death Mark
state_death_mark.description: Raises every kind of damage taken by 30% and pulls almost every attack onto the target. Lasts 2-3 actions.

state_perfect_focus.title: State: Perfect Focus
state_perfect_focus.description: Guarantees critical hits but reduces defense. It raises critical rate by 100% and lowers CON by 20%. It lasts 2-3 turns.

state_ethereal.title: State: Ethereal
state_ethereal.description: Physical damage passes through harmlessly, every magical element hits twice as hard. Lasts 3-5 turns.

state_life_link.title: State: Life Link
state_life_link.description: Damage taken is shared among all party members. Lasts 3-5 turns.

state_nausea.title: State: Nausea
state_nausea.description: Lowers AGI by 25%. Doesn't wear off on its own and lasts after battle.

state_drunk.title: State: Drunk
state_drunk.description: Drains 40% of max AP every turn. A solid hit or walking it off ends it. Lasts after battle.

state_infected.title: State: Infected
state_infected.description: Drains 10% of max HP every turn. Doesn't wear off on its own and lasts after battle.

state_floating.title: State: Floating
state_floating.description: It raises thunder damage taken 100%, raises STR by 10%, makes petro damage harmless and lowers physical damage taken 50%. It lasts 5 turns.

state_invisible.title: State: Invisible
state_invisible.description: It raises evasion by 999%, raises magic evasion by 999%, raises critical evasion by 999% and lowers how often it is targeted by 70%. It lasts 3 turns. A solid hit can break it early.

state_oily.title: State: Oily
state_oily.description: It raises fire damage taken 899%. It lasts 5 turns.

state_dodge.title: State: Dodge
state_dodge.description: It raises evasion by 200% and raises magic evasion by 200%. It lasts 1 turn.

state_withdrawal.title: State: Withdrawal
state_withdrawal.description: Lowers STR by 15%, INT by 15%, DEX by 10%, accuracy by 15% and evasion by 5%. Doesn't wear off on its own and lasts after battle.

state_grappled.title: State: Grappled
state_grappled.description: Held in a lock. Agility and evasion collapse and physical blows land harder. It lowers DEX by 60%, lowers evasion by 60% and raises physical damage taken by 25%. It lasts 2-3 turns.

state_pinned.title: State: Pinned
state_pinned.description: Pinned to the ground and unable to act. One solid hit shakes it loose. It lowers evasion by 90%. The afflicted cannot act at all. It lasts 1-2 turns. A solid hit can break it early.

state_guard_broken.title: State: Guard Broken
state_guard_broken.description: Their defence is prised open: defence halved and guarding does nothing. It lowers CON by 50%, lowers WIS by 20% and stops guarding entirely. It lasts 2 turns.

state_winded.title: State: Winded
state_winded.description: The breath is gone: slower, and no stamina builds up while it lasts. It lowers DEX by 20%, lowers AP charge rate by 65% and drains 5% of max MP every turn. It lasts 3 turns.

state_combo_ready.title: State: Combo Ready
state_combo_ready.description: The opening has been read and the follow-up is loaded. Some techniques hit far harder with it. It raises accuracy by 20% and raises critical rate by 15%. It lasts 2 turns.

state_vital_exposed.title: State: Vital Exposed
state_vital_exposed.description: A vital point is uncovered. Every physical blow that follows does half again as much. It raises physical damage taken by 50% and lowers critical evasion by 30%. It lasts 2-3 turns.

state_rooted_stance.title: State: Rooted Stance
state_rooted_stance.description: Planted and immovable: much harder to hurt or knock over, and slower for it. It raises CON by 40%, lowers DEX by 30% and wards off 3 different conditions. It lasts 4 turns.

state_flow_state.title: State: Flow State
state_flow_state.description: Reading the blow before it is thrown: turns attacks aside and answers some of them. It raises counter rate by 25%, raises evasion by 20% and lowers physical damage taken by 15%. It lasts 3 turns.

state_chi_burn.title: State: Chi Burn
state_chi_burn.description: The price of spending everything at once. The body keeps paying for a while. It drains 4% of max HP every turn, lowers INT by 15% and lowers AP charge rate by 50%. It lasts 3 turns.

state_concussed.title: State: Concussed
state_concussed.description: A blow to the head. Nothing aims true and nothing thinks straight. It lowers INT by 30%, lowers WIS by 30% and lowers accuracy by 20%. It lasts 2-3 turns.

lore_the_squishing.title: Lore: The Squishing
lore_the_squishing.description:
On 21 December 2012 the goddess of discord Eris will kill the goddess of justice Maat by hurling the Omega Tower at her. That has already happened, in the future. What reached us was the echo of the throw, sent twenty years back and across ninety-two dimensions, landing on 21 December 1992 in the sky of dimension three.

The paradox has been fraying the timeline ever since. Spacetime knots itself into local time-loop bubbles (see: the Rule of 80), and fragments of other dimensions collapse into this one, the Empty Empire of Varlenia foremost among them. By 2012, when the throw lands for real, the distortion is expected to leave this dimension uninhabitable.

It does not fall evenly. The higher a dimension's number, the faster it unravels: the Green Fields, dimension 77, are already mostly gone. The Omega Tower, driven into the earth by the same throw, is the one thing holding the ninety-two apart.

lore_the_rule_of_80.title: Lore: The Rule of 80
lore_the_rule_of_80.description:
Since the Squishing, anything moving faster than 80 kilometres an hour is pulled into the nearest time-loop bubble: a patch of spacetime, a few metres to hundreds of kilometres across, where the day resets at its end. Inside, the rule inverts. The only way out is to pass 80 again on the way out, and staying under it keeps you looping.

Bubbles are little more than a shimmer at close range, so road maps mark them. Their number and size have been growing since 1992.

Looping has its comforts. The only way to die for good inside one is to die above 80, or be struck by something that is; everything else resets. The cost is stagnation, and a looper keeps every previous day's memories while the world forgets.

No signal crosses a bubble's edge, electronic, mental or magical. Carrier pigeons fitted with USB drives manage 90 to 100 with a tailwind, which makes them the fastest reliable post between loops, and it is why the Truckers Society exists at all. Bubba's liminal engine is the one known way to drive straight through without slowing.

lore_the_encompassing_road.title: Lore: The Encompassing Road
lore_the_encompassing_road.description:
Every road in every world of the multiverse is, underneath, the same road. Bubba's liminal engine compresses the stretch ahead of a vehicle, and calibrated right it opens onto the Encompassing Road itself, where an ordinary exit can lead to another place, another dimension, another time, or the Scraps of Creation.

The road predates every driver on it. Trillions of years ago the concept of a road was born from the God of Asphalt, who paved the first one and became the first victim of a hit-and-run.

lore_the_mages_guild.title: Lore: The Mages Guild
lore_the_mages_guild.description:
Founded in 950 BC by King Solomon, the Mages Guild kept the world's hidden balance for millennia, until Margaret Thatcher revealed magic to the whole planet, live, by using it in the Falklands. In the early 1900s Sir Aleister Crowley refounded it under the British royal house as a pseudo-chivalric order, which is why its leadership still carries Sir and Lady.

Besides rebuilding lost technology with magic for the world's governments, the Guild exists to defend reality from what the Squishing lets in. Inside it is split into as many currents as there are schools of magic, but every major decision runs through the Three Pillars, who stand for past, present and future. In 2001 the seats belong to Sir Aleister Crowley, Lady Margaret Thatcher and 'the Father', Shoko Asahara.

A Pillar does not age while they hold the seat, and a term runs fifty years. Crowley has never stepped down, and nobody left in the Guild is in a position to make him.

lore_hypercapitalist_collective.title: Lore: Hypercapitalist Collective
lore_hypercapitalist_collective.description:
A pyramid scheme the size of a continent, running the trade between dimensions. Its members took the Rule of 80 and made it doctrine: stay above the threshold long enough and the body stops resetting even at a standstill. While the rest of the world loops and forgets, the Collective remembers.

That memory is the business model. They sell escapes to people trapped in loops and trade anything else, memories and emotions included. They also hold every source of clean water left; everything outside their reach is cut with LSD.

At open war with the Archive Foundation, whose radical transparency is bad for a trade empire built on leverage. Allied with the Gods.

lore_em,_the_memory_witch.title: Lore: Em, the Memory Witch
lore_em,_the_memory_witch.description:
Born in 1984 in Wimbledon, Britannia, wanting to be a witch in an age that had filed magic among the fairy tales. That changed when Margaret Thatcher, quietly a power broker in the Mages Guild, needed a focal point for the Solomon Ritual and picked her.

The price was 92% of her memories. They did not vanish; they were forged into the Spear of Memory, the weapon Eris later used to kill the Father aspect of YHWH. Em woke alone on Ritual Island on 1 January 2001 with no past she could reach and a power she is still learning to hold.

She has been on the road since, in a camper she shares with Bubba, heading to a meeting in Beagle she barely remembers agreeing to.

lore_camelcase_magic.title: Lore: CamelCase Magic
lore_camelcase_magic.description:
Every spell cast since the Squishing must be written and spoken in CamelCase: words run together, a capital opening each. FireBall works. 'Fire ball' does not, and saying it costs the caster. Two words is the working shape of a spell; three or more is reserved for the few that are powerful enough to earn the extra breath.

Multi-word formulas are a different tier: transcendentals, powerful enough to reshape reality on command, and the province of gods. A mortal who breaks a spell into separate words has the universe read it as an attempted transcendental and bill them for it, from the loss of their voice upward.

Grimoires make the rule visible. A spell written wrong infects the words beside it with copies of itself, and a book left unburned will eat whatever is next to it.

Active spells are chosen while the caster sleeps, each with its own cap on daily uses. Two in one slot fuse into a temporary spell for as long as it holds. Permanent versions of proven combinations can be bought from vending machines, or earned by ritual.
